properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2022 to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 957722
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in West Bethlehem Township, Washington County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/15/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in West Bethlehem Township, Washington county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/15/2023
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 8165816
Permit API: 125-23126
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: West Bethlehem Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/15/2023
Comments: On 11/15/2023, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Cowden 55 well. On 08/23/2023, a routine partial inspection was conducted (IR 3606258).On 08/23/2023, the tank onsite displayed oil which looked as thought it was dripping down the side fro the top. The oil was on a small section of gravel. A smaller section of oil was on another side of the tank. The operator was notified the day of observation. There were no violations issued on 08/23/2023 due to size of area impacted. During inspection on 11/15/2023, for following was observed: The site appeared remediated regarding the oil from the top of the tank; the operator removed the impacted gravel and placed it in a bucket marked with 08/24/2023. The bucket remianed onsite; I recommend that this is removed and disposed of a an approproate waste facility (Photos 1-4). It also looked as thought the operator had wiped the side of the tank off. During the followup, a conductivity test was performed underneath the lower valve on the tank, which displayed iron stained gravel. Conductivity readings within the iron stained gravel, under the valve, yielded elevated results (Photos 5-7).During the initial inspection, a gas odor was noticed near the wellhead and I informed the operator. They informed operation's to inspect. They informed me that the grey apparatus on the well (Photo 8) was part of the landowner's hookup. When the operator followed up, their gas meter did not detect any gas. During the 11/15/23 follow up, the odor was noticed again to which I informed the operator. They followed up the same day and mentioned that the heater on the landowner's setup was functioning properly and may be bleeding; they recommendded a pressure test be performed. I contacted the landowner to inform them of what Diversified (operator) informed me of - they also contacted the landowner. I contacted the landowner about my conversation with the operator and recommended that the setup receives maintenance. The operator informed me that they thought the odor contained mercaptan and may be coming from a Columbia gas line nearby. Below the wellsite is a Williams station that the gas flows to. Regarding the elevated conductivity observed onsite below the valve of the production tank, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.66(b)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/27/2025 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Troy Township, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/23/2025
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8235125
Permit API: 015-23893
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Felt liner (130 mil thickness) went down first, then wood/steel mats. Fine gravel is used to fill gaps between the mats.Precision Drilling 110 started drilling 4 new Marcellus wells at this site on April 1 2025, and expect to finish drilling around June 10, 2025. There are also 4 existing Marcellus wells here. They drill on water based mud for the vertical section, then switch to diesel based mud for the kickoff (curve) and horizontal section.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site to comply with 102.22 Permanent Stabilization. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies. Pooled water on the pad surface in 3 separate puddles has electrical conductivity (EC) of 0.68-1.7 mS/cm with an Oakton PCTS5.62FJLP

Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. The well name and API was scratched into a pipe clamp, this does not meet the posting requirements of 3211(G). The line leading to the production tank appears to have failed and separated. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks. Gas was leaking from the base of the wellhead as seen in the attached photographs at 12%LEL. The line leading into the production tank appears to have separated and was leaking gas at 79%Gas. The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department. 78.88(d) - Failure to notify the Department and take corrective action to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion or other signs of deterioration that compromises the integrity of the well. 78.73(a) - Failure to operate the well in accordance with 25 PA code Chapter 78 and ensure the integrity of the well is maintained. 78.74 - Venting of gas to the atmosphere that produces a hazard to public health and safety.

Comments: On March 10, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Range Resource's Shearer Robert pad located in Robinson Township, Washington County following IR 4132845, where the Department issued violations for a 193 gallon release of produced water onto the graveled pad.IR 4161502 documents the 2/18/2026 received NOV response from Range Resources.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox was an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the approximately 100 ft x 20 ft area of the gravel pad where the spill occurred. Permit API: 047-24934
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/12/2024
Comments: I conducted this inspection in response to a spill that was self reported by Seneca. Seneca discovered three pin holes in the produced water line coming from the E08L pad. Approximately 10'x 20' x3' of soil was impacted by the release of produced water. Jeff Passarello from Seneca estimated that 25 gallons had been released from the compromised line. The leak was found during routine inspection of the line. At the time of my arrival crews had replaced the compromised section of the above ground produced water line and the excavated dirt was placed into 3 short containment boxes. These boxes are being temporarily stored inside of secondary containment on the E08L pad. Field conductivity probes were used to verify the impacted soil had been removed. Conductivity readings throughout the remediated area are comparable to background levels. 30-40 feet of brush was cleared to gain access to the failed section of pipe. A third party contractor was pulling up with a load of mulch and seed to temporarily stabilize the recent earth disturbance while I was on site.All removed soil will be disposed of at an approved facility pending lab results. Please provide proof of this materials disposal to The Department when it becomes available.

The quantity of oil spilled is unknown, but appears to be greater than 5 gallons and less than one barrel. Oil stained soil with absorbent peat is noted in an L shape approximately 10 feet wide and 30 feet long that extends to the edge of the location. Spring melt allowed the material to run to the edge of the site. Per the operator, the employee is no longer with the company. Cleanup should be completed in the next few days. Followup inspection will be performed at that time.The operator was also asked about the steep and rutted access roads on this lease and said that they have recently acquired a new bulldozer and intend to grade and fix lease roads soon.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 852791
Permit API: 117-21998
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-06-14
Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess conditions on and off the pad. Both the 2H and 4H wells continue to flow back. A puddle in front of the west containment next to the MASS had a conductivity of 16.6 mS/cm. Another puddle to the south, not directly in front of the containment, had a conductivity of 4.96 mS/cm. Soil conductivity readings in this area ranged from 1.3 to >4 mS/cm when measured with the soil conductivity meter. On the main pad surface, the conductivity of puddles on the surface near the gravel piles remains elevated with conductivities above 2 mS/cm here. The area between the well heads, which had elevated conductivities during the previous inspection, has been back-filled with new gravel. After speaking with Taylor Parsons of Falcon on site about my conductivity readings, he accompanied me to the MASS. I showed him that the Oakton conductivity meter was showing that the puddles in front and to the south of the west containment were elevated. I took a conductivity reading of the fluid inside the containment which was >19.99 mS/cm. He stated that the containment may not be adequate for preventing spills of produced water to the surface when water trucks are off-loading the MASS. He said that he would have a more substantial area of containment built which would allow the trucks to drive onto the containment, which he believed would prevent produced water from getting onto the surface of the MASS pad. A contractor, Blood Hound, was on site when I arrived. The contractor marked the location of the PVC Pipe with spray paint and flags. The path is included as a red line in the map in photo #3. The attached maps and tables show the conductivity readings recorded during this inspection. Outstanding violations.

Comments: On August 13, 2025, the Department conducted a Site Restoration inspection of the Diversified's Diamond 4 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Westmoreland County following the receipt of a Well Site Restoration resubmission the Department received on 5/20/2025 and an updated version of this resubmission which was received on 5/29/2025. Prior WSRR submissions were submitted on 7/25/2024 and 4/4/2025, however both were administratively incomplete and denied. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/7/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 12/7/2024. In addition, according to Department records the well site was restored as of 11/21/2024 (documented in IR 3876070), therefore the resubmitted WSRR was not submitted within 60 days of restoration.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Erosion and Sediment Control Plan for the Diamond 4 plugged well site to be fixed on the access road gate. The access road to the Diamond 4 well site was observed to be comprised of gravel and compacted soil. This access road is proposed to remain as it also services a compressor station. The Department traveled to the approximate GPS coordinate location of the plugged well and observed the plugged well site to be exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No erosion or sedimentation issues were observed nor were any fluid leaks or fluid discharges observed. All erosion and sediment control features appeared to be removed from the well site.Based on today's inspection, the Department recommends the Well Site Restoration Report Submission be approved at this time. In addition, violations for failure to submit a WSRR within 60 days of restoration of the plugged well site is being noted as immediately corrected at this time. Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an inspection app IT error.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Blackhill Energy's Nichols A (1H) well site located in Smithfield Township, Bradford County on 7/29/2024 at 1120 hours. The weather was 77 degrees F with mostly clear skies. The inspection was conducted in response to a discovered release reported by the operator. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #382564 is tied to this release within CTS.On 7/29/2024 at ~0815 hours, Blackhill Energy discovered a produced water release to the pad surface at their Nichols (A) well site. The release appeared to come from a water truck after or during recovering water from the produced water tank onsite. Blackhill Energy is unsure of the total amount of the release. Moody and Associates, Fenton Transport/Trucking, and Blackhill Energy representatives were all present during my visit. During my inspection, the overview of the release area was observed. Some portions of the pad surface within the release area were damp but no standing or pooled water was present in the area. White colored staining and/or crystals were observed in the area. Soil within the area of the release was field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) with a Hanna Groline Soil Conductivity Meter and returned a reading of >4.0mS/cm (photo #4). Soils within the stormwater channels along the edges of the pad were field measured for EC below 1.0mS/cm. All other soils, pad materials and pooled water field measured on the pad surface, outside of the release area were field measured for EC below 1.0mS/cm. No evidence was observed that would suggest any portion of the release escaped the outlined release area. Blackhill Energy reported that the release would have occurred when a water truck was offloading from the produced water tank onsite on 7/27/2024. It was believed that foam from the produced water was able to escape from the vent on the side of the truck. A waste container for impacted material was en route to the site when I departed. Excavation activities were set to begin upon arrival of the waste container.Based on the findings of this inspection report and the reported release of an unknown quantity of produced water outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #015-21167 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)35 P.S. 6018.301I departed the site at 1215 hours.

Comments: On May 2, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the MCC West Well Site in Jefferson Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a fluid release reported by the Operator on 5/1/2022. According to the report approximately 50-60 gallons of condensate oil was released to the well pad when a load line on a truck failed. The release was discovered on 5/1/22 at 8:10am and reported to the Department spill hot line on 5/1/22 at 9:46am. At the time of inspection, The Act 9 site ID sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site. Three roll off disposal boxes were staged on the east corner of the well pad. The roll off boxes were labeled as Non-Hazardous Waste condensate impacted material and dated 5/1/22. The impacted area appeared to be directly adjacent to the brine tank secondary containment location. The impacted area appeared to be 40’ in length and approximately 15’ wide with a maximum depth of approximately 12 inches. No discharge was observed off the well pad and the spill did not appear to impact waters of the commonwealth. Violations are being issued for failure to control a regulated fluid resulting a release to the ground.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protetion (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 145 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 2/18/21 @ 1130 hours. The weather was 16 degree and sunny. Snow with a coating of ice has accumulated on the site. Joe Harrick and Ron Burdick of JKLM and Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consulting were present onsite for the inspections. On 2/13/21, Mr. Harrick called to report a release of 80-120 gallons of production fluid on the Headwaters 145 Well Pad. JKLM was in the process of transferring fluid from the production tanks to the Headwaters Tank Farm, when a hose connected to the pump let loose releasing the fluid to the containment and the pad surface. A nearby vac truck was able to remove the standing liquid from the contaiment and the well pad, estimated to be approximately 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, JKLM has removed the majority of the impacted pad material. An excavated area approximately 15' x 20' was observed on the Northeast side of the well pad located between the permanent tan-colored production tanks and the green-colored extra storage tanks. The excavation is between 6" and 24" deep. The excavation was impeded by frozen ground conditions and the location of buried dump lines. Some "hand work" was done to remove material around the above ground port for the waterline use to transfer the production fluid to the tank farm. At the time of the spill the E&S discharge points at the corners of the well pad were shut-in. JKLM stated no production fluid entered the E&S controls or left the site. A total of 8 rolloff containers of impacted snow, ice and pad material have been removed from the site. JKLM believes the majority of impacted material has been excavated. JKLM stated they plan to replace all existing hoses onsite to discourage a similar event. Penn E&R will be onsite to conduct confirmatory samples when weather allows. Due to the volume of the release, JKLM confirmed they plan to demonstrate attainment of Act 2 standards. This release is referred to the DEP Cleanups and Brownfields Program. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a57 I departed the site at 1315 hours.

Comments: On 1/11/23 a follow-up inspection of the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well site was conducted related to violations issued on 10/24/22 (IR: 3445085) and outstanding violations issued on 11/23/22 (IR: 3462090).Background:On 10/24/22, during a routine inspection, violations were issued for a brine release at the Cartier/Luxner 4 OG Well Site (IR: 3445085). Elevated conductivity was observed inside the earthen containment berm that surrounds the production tank. An operator response was received by the Department on 11/8/22 stating that the impacted material was removed and disposed of, and a new tank had been installed. On 11/23/22 a follow-up inspection was conducted and elevated conductivity was still observed in soil inside of the containment berm for the production tank (IR: 3462090). Outstanding violations were issued.Findings:-The area that exhibited elevated conductivity due to a leak in the corroded tank appeared to have been remediated. No elevated conductivity readings were obtained in that area of the containment (Photo #1). -The new tank was not hooked up to the well. -The pipe that had previously been attached to the old tank was not capped off (Photo #2), and a slow drip of fluid was observed coming from the pipe and hitting the ground below.-The substrate that was below the leaking pipe was stained and exhibited elevated conductivity (Photos #3-4).I informed Bryan Goletz of Diversified of my findings. According to Diversified in the NOV response dated 11/8/22 related to the first violations issued on 10/24/22, "The tank was not in service at the time of the inspection and the well doesn't produce fluid when in production". However, the fluid in the old tank during the initial inspection was at least shoulder height. And fluid is slowly, yet actively dripping from the pipe that should terminate at the tank. Outstanding violations of 78.57(a) and 78.54 are being issued.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/16/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/16/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 959605
Permit API: 081-21884
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/16/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted due to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 15 gallons of hydraulic oil from a crane while it was traveling from the B pad to the A pad on the night of 6/15/22. I met with company man Walt Arnold on Pad B initially. He informed me that the access road had already been scraped the night before to remove the hydraulic oil from the access roads of Pads A and B. We then traveled to Pad A where he showed me the crane which was sitting on secondary containment. Next we each traveled back to the B Pad and along the way I stopped several times to inspect the access road. No hydraulic oil was observed on the access road. On pad B, I first inspected the area of the pad which had been impacted by the release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water on 6/9/22. More fluid was present on the pad surface, as well as on the secondary containment, than was present during the inspection the previous day. Mr. Arnold informed me that it had rained heavily overnight. The fluid in this area of the pad had an electrical conductivity (EC) below 800 uS/cm as measured in several spots. The EC in the sump in the stormwater channel was 742 uS/cm. The EC at the channel outlet at the corner of the pad was 865 uS/cm. Two other areas of the pad appeared to have elevated EC readings. Puddles on the pad surface near the upright produced water tanks closest to the freshwater tank had an EC of 1.8 mS/cm. More puddles on the pad surface near the secondary containment where the coiled tubing unit had been rigged up had an EC of 5.6 mS/cm. The fluid on the secondary containment here had an EC of 9.8 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was in the process of sucking up the fluid from this section of secondary containment. Violations noted for the hydraulic oil release and considered immediately corrected.
